name: AR-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Rick Crawford running with large cash advantage
model.rationale: Crawford is a well-funded incumbent in a deeply Republican district, while Terri Green has raised almost nothing and has no meaningful outside support. Markets and fundamentals both point to a comfortable Republican win, so the forecast stays near the baseline.
model.watch: Any late surge in Democratic spending or a major scandal involving Crawford could narrow the margin, though an upset remains very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rick Crawford seeks another term in this heavily Republican northeastern Arkansas district, where the partisan lean favors Republicans by more than twenty points. He enters the general election with over a million dollars on hand after raising nearly a million during the cycle. Democrat Terri Green has raised only about $65,000 and had under $12,000 on hand, leaving her little capacity to communicate with voters. A Libertarian candidate, Steve Parsons, is also on the ballot but has shown no measurable campaign activity.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the fundraising gap, and prediction markets, which price Crawford's chances around 97 percent. The expected result is a decisive Republican victory, with Green needing an extraordinary shift in the political environment to make the race competitive.
